dimensions.definition: What naturally attracts or motivates a person when an activity, relationship, or goal is already going well.
What is naturally less attractive because it lacks a governed motivational reward, without implying fear, pathology, incompetence, or moral disapproval.
How immediate progress, emerging possibility, continuity over time, and dependable future preparation shape preference.
Why a person prefers ownership, exploratory freedom, dependable collaboration, or clear role structure.
What makes achievement or contribution feel meaningfully acknowledged or satisfying.
How scarce time, attention, energy, opportunity, space, or effort is naturally allocated among legitimate alternatives.
What combination of challenge, variety, connection, clarity, autonomy, pace, or stability makes an environment naturally attractive.
Why trust grows through results, openness and possibility, relational continuity, or evidence and reliability.
What governed signal naturally causes a person to revisit a decision already made.
What governed signal makes an activity, decision, conversation, or responsibility feel sufficiently complete.
